---
title: "Formatting & helpers"
---

Use Python formatters when you need **text**, D3 format strings when an Altair
axis or tooltip expects **`format`**, and a Vega expression when an axis expects
**`labelExpr`**. Keep chart data numeric or temporal so sorting and scales work.

| Helper | Returns | Where to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `format_number(1234567)` | `"1.2M"` | Python labels, captions, or a separate text column |
| `format_date("2023-01-15")` | `"Jan-23"` | Python labels or an ordinal date column |
| `d3_number_format(decimals=0)` | `",.0f"` | `alt.Axis(format=...)`, `alt.Tooltip(format=...)`, template `value_format` |
| `d3_date_format("month_year")` | `"%b-%y"` | Temporal axis/tooltip `format`, template `date_format` |
| `vega_scale_labelExpr()` | Vega expression | `alt.Axis(labelExpr=...)` for automatic K/M/B ticks |

All chart examples below use this illustrative data:

```{python}
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
import attaviz

attaviz.enable()

data = pd.DataFrame({
    "date": pd.to_datetime(["2023-01-01", "2023-04-01", "2023-07-01", "2023-10-01"]),
    "funding": [1_200_000, 1_500_000, 1_350_000, 1_800_000],
    "completion": [0.25, 0.45, 0.62, 0.86],
})
```

## Number formatting

`format_number()` returns text using WBG automatic scale suffixes (K/M/B),
precision based on the scaled magnitude, and optional currency, percent, or units.

```{python}
print(attaviz.format_number(1234567))                   # 1.2M
print(attaviz.format_number(1234))                      # 1,234
print(attaviz.format_number(0.456, percent=True))        # 45.6%
print(attaviz.format_number(50000, currency=True))       # $50.0K
print(attaviz.format_number(1234567890, unit="bytes"))   # 1.2GB
print(attaviz.format_number(1234567, scale="M", decimals=2))  # 1.23M
```

- `decimals` — integer or `"auto"` (default): 2 decimals below 1, 1 below 100,
  otherwise 0, applied after scaling. Zero displays as `0`.
- `scale` — `"K"`, `"M"`, `"B"`, `"G"`, or `"auto"`. Automatic scaling starts
  at 10,000 (K), 1,000,000 (M), and 1,000,000,000 (B).
- `currency=True` — prefix with `$`.
- `percent=True` — multiply a fraction by 100 and append `%`.
- `unit` — append a unit; technical units (`watt`, `byte`, `bit`, `ton`, ...)
  use G for billions.
- Missing values (`None` or float NaN) display as `N/A`.

For a formatted tooltip, add a text column while keeping the numeric column
for the scale:

```{python}
labeled = data.assign(funding_label=data["funding"].map(attaviz.format_number))

alt.Chart(labeled).mark_bar().encode(
    x="date:T",
    y="funding:Q",
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("date:T"), alt.Tooltip("funding_label:N", title="Funding")],
).properties(width=600, height=240)
```

## D3 number format strings

`d3_number_format()` returns a format specification; it does not format a value.
Pass that specification to both the axis and tooltip:

```{python}
number_format = attaviz.d3_number_format(decimals=0, currency=True)  # $,.0f

alt.Chart(data).mark_bar().encode(
    x="date:T",
    y=alt.Y("funding:Q", title="Funding (USD)", axis=alt.Axis(format=number_format)),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("funding:Q", title="Funding", format=number_format)],
).properties(width=600, height=240)
```

For percentages, pass fractions: `0.45` displays as `45.0%` with `.1%`.

```{python}
attaviz.line(
    data,
    x="date",
    y="completion",
    value_format=attaviz.d3_number_format(percent=True, decimals=1),
    date_format=attaviz.d3_date_format("month_year"),
    title="Completion increased during the year",
    width=600,
    height=240,
)
```

`d3_number_format(scale="M")` does **not** divide values or append M; its `scale`
argument is unused. To display millions, explicitly divide the data and label
the axis “Funding (millions)”. For automatic K/M/B suffixes, use the expression
helper below. The Python helper's `currency=True` always means `$`; template
`value_format="currency", currency="USD"` uses a currency code instead.

## Auto-scaled Altair axis labels

`vega_scale_labelExpr()` applies WBG K/M/B suffixes to raw numbers per tick.
It returns an expression for `labelExpr`, while tooltips can still show exact
values with a D3 format string:

```{python}
alt.Chart(data).mark_bar().encode(
    x="date:T",
    y=alt.Y(
        "funding:Q",
        title="Funding (USD)",
        axis=alt.Axis(labelExpr=attaviz.vega_scale_labelExpr(currency=True)),
    ),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("funding:Q", format=attaviz.d3_number_format(currency=True))],
).properties(width=600, height=240)
```

Set `unit="bytes"` for unit suffixes (including G at billions) or `decimals=2`
for fixed precision. Pass this expression to `labelExpr`, not `format`.

## Date formatting

`format_date()` accepts a Python `date`, `datetime`, or ISO date string and
returns text. The WBG fiscal year runs July–June: July 2023 belongs to FY24.

```{python}
from datetime import date

d = date(2023, 1, 15)
for style in ["day", "month", "month_year", "quarter", "year", "fiscal_year"]:
    print(style, attaviz.format_date(d, style=style),
          attaviz.format_date(d, style=style, short=False))

print(attaviz.format_date("2023-07-01", style="fiscal_year"))  # FY24
```

Use `short=False` for full month names and four-digit years. Short quarters use
`23Q1`; long quarters use `2023Q1`. Python's short day style is day/month/year
(`15/1/2023`).

## D3 date format strings

`d3_date_format()` supports `"day"`, `"month"`, `"month_year"`, and `"year"`.
Use a temporal encoding (`:T`) and pandas datetime values. Here the axis uses
month/year and the tooltip shows a full date:

```{python}
alt.Chart(data).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X(
        "date:T",
        title=None,
        axis=alt.Axis(format=attaviz.d3_date_format("month_year")),
    ),
    y="funding:Q",
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("date:T", title="Date", format=attaviz.d3_date_format("day", short=False)),
        alt.Tooltip("funding:Q", title="Funding", format=attaviz.d3_number_format(decimals=0)),
    ],
).properties(width=600, height=240)
```

`short=False` changes `%b-%y` (`Jan-23`) to `%B %Y` (`January 2023`). The D3
short day format is `%m/%d/%Y` (`01/15/2023`), which differs from the Python
formatter's day/month/year output.

Quarter and fiscal-year styles raise `ValueError` in `d3_date_format()`.
Precompute them with `format_date()` and use an ordinal (`:O`) encoding to
preserve data order. This custom Altair chart works with quarter strings;
`attaviz.line()` requires numeric or temporal x values.

```{python}
quarterly = data.assign(
    quarter=data["date"].map(lambda d: attaviz.format_date(d, style="quarter"))
)

alt.Chart(quarterly).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X("quarter:O", sort=None, title="Quarter"),
    y="funding:Q",
    tooltip=["quarter:O", alt.Tooltip("funding:Q", format=",.0f")],
).properties(width=600, height=240)
```

## Captions

Use [`frame()`](charts.qmd#publication-frame) for notes, source, byline, and
an accessibility description. That reference includes a complete rendered
example with a visible title and subtitle.

`add_caption()` attaches a single styled caption. Supply your own “Source:”
or “Note:” prefix, and use `\n` for multiple lines:

```{python}
chart = attaviz.line(data, x="date", y="completion", value_format="percent", width=600)
attaviz.add_caption(
    chart,
    "Source: illustrative example data.\nNote: completion is a fraction of participants.",
    align="left",
)
```

`align` accepts `"left"` (default, WBG alignment), `"center"`, or `"right"`.
Like `frame()`, `add_caption()` wraps the chart and changes responsive width to
600 px. Apply either helper after adding layers or hover; use one footer helper
per chart.
